title: Method doc tooltip miss indicate return enum value's class name(inconsistent with the method auto-completion tooltip)
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.5.1stable ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7628) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12490F (12 threads) - 31.81 GiB memory ### Issue description When using a method that returns an enumeration value, I found that it lacked a prompt for the class name to which the enumeration belongs, this will cause confusion when calling methods between classes have similar enumeration names. For example, if you have a Class named `Fruit` with an enumeration named `Type` representing the category of the fruit, and also you have anther Class named `Knife` with an enumeration named `Type` representing the category of the knife. Then, somewhere(e.g. a script which also has a `Type` enumeration) you have a function which return a fruit(or knife) instance's type(the example I gave may not be very appropriate, as you can always define a enumeration type variable named type for these classes and directly obtain the instance's category through access type variable). But, at this point, checking the document tooltips for those methods must confuse you(u can't distinguish the class enumeration Type belongs to, of course, you can always go to the definition by clicking on the enumeration name to view the class it belongs to, but this is not very intuitive). On the other hand, although you can solve this problem by always using different enumeration names, such as naming them `FruitType`(or `KnifeType`), this will increase the workload. But what I want to express is that when calling this function that returns an enumeration value, the documentation tooltip does not display the name of the class to which the enumeration belongs. It only simply displays something like `function_name ()-> Type` or `function_name_with_enum_para(para: Type) -> Type` **This behavior is inconsistent with the method auto-completion tooltip.** The following is the feature of the method auto-completion tooltips: - When you call those method using a script instance without class_name, the method auto-completion tooltip will display `script_name.gd enum_name function_name()` such as `my_node.gd.Type get_type()` - When you call those method using a script instance with class_name, the method auto-completion tooltip will display `class_name.gd enum_name function_name()` such as `MyNode.Type get_type()` - Also, when you call some method has enum parameters, method auto-completion will display the enum parameter's class name belongs to, like `MyNode.Type get_type_by_enum_para(para: MyNode.Type)` For the script where the enumeration definition is located, we can use enumeration names directly in function parameters or return values, omitting class name(This is reasonable because they are currently in the same class/domain, the code can be omitted), but whenever calling a function that using the enumeration value(whether as a parameter or a return value), I think the name of the enumeration class name belongs to must always be displayed in doc tooltips, just like the method auto-completion tooltip. It is reasonable to unify their behavior. #### Screenshots: **Attention: caller in the screenshot is always `my_node.gd`** _auto-completion tooltip examples(no omit class name, very clear):_ call self's function call other script's function _doc tooltip examples(no matter who the caller is, always omit class name, make confusion):_ call self's function call other script's function #### Demo: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94134eeb-b84b-4fba-a2ed-8022e9a738f5 ### Steps to reproduce N/A ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [issue_2025-10-27_00-39-50.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23151267/issue_2025-10-27_00-39-50.zip)
